issues.description: nevra[0] uses the first character of the filename including potential leading digits, which mismatches Koji's lowercase-letter directory layout
issues.detail: Koji's canonical path uses the first character of the package name (e.g., 'g' for 'glibc'), not the first character of the full NEVRA filename. Many RPMs filenames begin with a letter so this often works, but packages like '389-ds-base' or any name starting with a digit will produce a path like '/3/389-ds-base-...rpm' which does not match Koji's layout and will 404.

issues.description: extract_arch_from_url can return None and the caller does not handle it
issues.detail: If the URL doesn't contain a known arch (e.g., a noarch package whose URL embeds 'noarch'), extract_arch_from_url returns None. The constructed URL becomes '.../latest/None/Packages/...' which silently produces a broken URL rather than failing loudly. Either handle noarch explicitly or raise on no match.

issues.description: Race condition between bump-lockfile merge and coreos-koji-tagger acknowledged but not mitigated
issues.detail: The PR description admits the crafted coreos-pool URLs may not exist until coreos-koji-tagger runs. If Konflux fetches before tagging completes, the build fails with 404s and no retry/verification logic exists in this script. Consider at minimum a comment pointing to the operational runbook, or a verification step.

issues.description: Arch list is hardcoded and duplicates information available elsewhere
issues.detail: The arches list ['x86_64', 'aarch64', 'ppc64le', 's390x'] is hardcoded in extract_arch_from_url. If a new arch is added (e.g., riscv64), this function silently breaks. Consider deriving from the same source the rest of the script uses or at least adding a comment linking the two lists.

issues.description: Word-boundary regex may match arch substrings appearing earlier in URL paths
issues.detail: The regex matches the first occurrence of an arch token in the URL. If a mirror path or repo name happens to contain an arch string before the actual package arch segment, the wrong arch is returned. Anchoring to the path segment just before the filename would be safer.

issues.description: Stale comment about prioritizing coreos-pool URL remains after logic changes
issues.detail: Line 160 still says 'Prioritize the url from fedora-coreos-pool' but the surrounding explanatory comment about the DNF5 bug was removed. With the new approach rewriting all URLs to coreos-pool post-hoc, this prioritization is largely redundant; either remove or update the comment to reflect why it's still useful.

review.summary: The patch rewrites non-coreos-pool URLs into a crafted Koji canonical path to work around DNF5 issue 2466. The main concerns are correctness of the path construction (nevra[0] for the directory prefix is wrong for names starting with digits, and noarch URLs would yield 'None' in the path), and an unmitigated race with coreos-koji-tagger. Minor cleanups around stale comments and hardcoded arch list would also help. Overall direction is reasonable but a couple of edge cases need handling before merge.
